correctness.rationale: The neighborhood of every vertex in part \(V_i\) is exactly the union of all other parts. Therefore an empty label is legal exactly when each color occurs outside \(V_i\), which is the stated support-set criterion. Partitioning labelings by the four per-part counts then gives the multinomial weight enumerator without omission or multiplicity. The minimum-weight cases \(m=1,2,3\) and \(m\ge4\) follow from explicit constructions and the necessary number of outside part-color incidences. As an independent bounded check, direct brute force on representative multipartite profiles including \((1,1),(1,3),(2,2),(3,4),(4,4),(5,2)\) reproduced \(\gamma_{r2}=\min\{4,\max\{2,m\}\}\). The finite check is corroborative only; the neighborhood argument proves the arbitrary-order statement.
risks: The result is specific to ordinary two-color rainbow domination on connected complete multipartite graphs; it does not classify higher-color or proper variants.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge originality survives. The foundational 2010 paper defines the same invariant and proves general extremal bounds but does not treat complete multipartite graphs or an all-function generating polynomial. Fresh Resultary searches returned the audited record itself plus distinct Roman/rainbow-related domination records, not a prior theorem implying the exact profile criterion or weight enumerator. The scalar minimum could conceivably have appeared elsewhere; originality is attached to the stronger all-function classification and enumerator.
